analysis.title: Pinterest: De Minimis Change De Maximus Consequence
key_insights: PINS 3Q26 revenue grew 12% y/y, below DB's 15% estimate and the low end of the company's 13%-15% guidance. This breaks the recent pattern of results beating the high end of guidance.
4Q26 revenue growth guidance of 8%-12% is well below DB's prior 16.6% estimate and consensus of 14.9%. The guided range widened to five points from three points in 3Q.
3Q Adj. EBITDA was $339mn, below the $345mn guidance midpoint. The 4Q Adj. EBITDA guidance midpoint of $563mn is below DB/Street estimates of $609mn/$606mn.

The de minimis regulatory change had a larger impact than expected, but DB does not think it fully explains the 4Q outlook. Europe faces a 17-point easier comparison, the sales force disruption appears to be reversing, the regulatory change was already in effect throughout 3Q, and mix shifts toward the larger U.S. business.

4Q growth is guided broadly in line with 3Q despite factors that should support sequential improvement. DB reads this as a possible additional drag on advertiser demand and has less confidence in the near-term growth trajectory.

DB channel checks were cautious on 4Q. Higher interest rates, persistent inflation and elevated gas prices weighed on advertiser expectations. Pinterest may be seeing the pressure earlier or more acutely than peers.
Competitive intensity may be a factor, particularly as Meta's improving ad products give advertisers another scaled-performance channel.
European revenue declined about 50bps y/y after growing 12% in 2Q. MAUs rose 7% but ARPU fell 7.5% as the de minimis change and go-to-market restructuring weighed on monetization.

The de minimis change, which ended the duty exemption for shipments valued at or below €150, was an 11-point headwind to European revenue growth and drove most of the consolidated miss. The company-level impact was about 3 points versus the 1 point assumed in guidance.

Growth in the core European enterprise business fell about 50% sequentially during the sales force transition to the Performance+ model. 4Q-to-date growth in this business has recovered above the 2Q level, but overall European growth is tracking in line with 3Q.
U.S. and Canada revenue grew 14% y/y, down from 18% in 2Q, on 4% MAU growth and 10% ARPU growth. World Cup and Prime Day timing explained part of the slowdown.
Food and beverage advertising remains soft globally, partly offset by strength in pharma. The U.S. advertiser base is more diversified than in the past, which limits exposure to any single vertical.

Global MAUs rose 10% to 661mn. Gen Z is 57% of users, and UCAN Gen Z ARPU is comparable to Millennials. About 80% of Pinterest Assistant searches are commercial, versus more than half across the platform.
Visual Search Ads, app installs, additional programmatic demand and deeper SMB penetration each address meaningful budget pools, but all are early and will take time to scale.

DB cut its 4Q26 revenue estimate to $1,470mn (+11% y/y) from $1,533mn and its Adj. EBITDA estimate to $578mn from $609mn. This is consistent with reiterated guidance of about 30% FY26 Adj. EBITDA margin.
DB cut FY27 revenue to $5.3bn (+12% y/y, 2.5% below prior), Adj. EBITDA to $1.57bn from $1.66bn (29% margin vs 30% prior) and EPS to $2.26 from $2.47.
Price target cut to $23 from $24, based on 9x FY27 Adj. EBITDA. The rating stays Hold with the stock at $19.36.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $23 from $24 at 9x FY27 Adj. EBITDA after a 3Q revenue miss and weak 4Q guidance. Hold rating maintained.

sector_views.rationale: Channel checks were cautious on 4Q advertiser budgets given higher rates, inflation and gas prices. Meta's improving ad products add competitive pressure.

earnings_insights: PINS 3Q26 reported revenue growth was 12% y/y versus DB's 15% estimate and company guidance of 13%-15%.
PINS 3Q26 Adj. EBITDA reported at $339mn versus the $345mn guidance midpoint.

PINS 4Q26 guidance: revenue growth of 8%-12% y/y ($1,425-1,475mn) versus DB's prior estimate of 16.6% and consensus of 14.9%. Adj. EBITDA guidance is $538-588mn (midpoint $563mn) versus prior DB/Street estimates of $609mn/$606mn.
DB's revised 4Q26 estimates: revenue $1,470mn (+11% y/y) from $1,533mn, Adj. EBITDA $578mn from $609mn.
DB's revised FY27 estimates: revenue $5.3bn (+12% y/y), Adj. EBITDA $1.57bn (29% margin) from $1.66bn, EPS $2.26 from $2.47.
The company reiterated guidance for about 30% FY26 Adj. EBITDA margin.
Regional 3Q26: Europe revenue fell about 50bps y/y (2Q: +12%) with ARPU down 7.5% and MAU up 7%. U.S. and Canada revenue rose 14% y/y (2Q: +18%) with MAU up 4% and ARPU up 10%.
risk_factors: The de minimis change (end of the duty exemption for shipments of €150 or less) is a larger and more persistent cross-border headwind than the company assumed.
Advertiser demand may be weakening further in 4Q from higher interest rates, persistent inflation and elevated gas prices.
Competition from Meta's improving ad products.
The wider guidance range (five points versus three) signals lower visibility.
Sales force restructuring in Europe is still disrupting the core enterprise business.
Food and beverage ad softness is global.

tension_points.bull_case: Engagement is strong: global MAUs +10% to 661mn, Gen Z is 57% of users, and about 80% of Pinterest Assistant searches are commercial versus more than half across the platform. DB says this supports the case that Pinterest owns differentiated, high-intent shopping behavior.
tension_points.bear_case: Revenue growth is slowing (12% in 3Q, 8%-12% guided for 4Q) from de minimis effects in Europe, softer U.S. growth, cautious advertiser budgets and Meta competition. The new ad formats are early and will take time to scale.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fourth-quarter revenue growth landing at or below the low end of the 8%-12% guide would undercut the view that the shortfall is mostly de minimis-related and temporary.
